preconditions.expression: T == int(stdin.split()[0]) and T >= 1 and T <= 5
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer T (1 ≤ T ≤ 5) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(S) >= 1 and len(S) <= 10**5 and all('a' <= c <= 'z' for c in S) for S in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]])
preconditions.description: Each test case's first line is a string S of length N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10^5) consisting of lowercase English letters ('a' to 'z').

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= K <= len(S) for S, K_line in zip([line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
preconditions.description: Each test case's second line is an integer K (1 ≤ K ≤ N) representing the desired subsequence length.

postconditions.expression: all(len(output_line) == K for S, K, output_line in zip([line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [int(line.strip()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line has exactly length K.

postconditions.expression: all(all(S[i] == output_line[j] for j, i in enumerate(selected_indices)) for S, K, output_line, selected_indices in zip([line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [int(line.strip()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]], stdout.splitlines(), [sorted([i for i, c in enumerate(S) if c in output_line])]))
postconditions.description: The output line is a subsequence of S, meaning its characters appear in S in the same order (though not necessarily consecutively).

postconditions.expression: all(output_line == min([S[i1] + S[i2] + ... + S[iK] for i1 in range(len(S)) if i1 < i2 < ... < iK < len(S) for i2 in range(i1+1, len(S)) for ... for iK in range(iK_prev+1, len(S))], key=lambda x: x) for S, K, output_line in zip([line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [int(line.strip()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output line is the lexicographically smallest subsequence of S of length K. Lexicographical order is determined by comparing characters from left to right at the first differing position.
